paragraphs: The M60 is remembered from film more than from service, and the two versions are not the same weapon. Carried at the hip it is cinema; used properly it sits on a bipod with a second soldier feeding the belt, which is how it was actually meant to work.
The model holds 61,823 polygons and 63,377 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, game weapons, film props, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The decorated skull is not a memento mori in the European sense. In the Mexican tradition it is celebratory, worn and painted for a day when the dead are welcomed back rather than mourned, and dressing one as a musician is entirely in keeping with that.
The model holds 48,177 polygons and 48,164 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits cultural and festival visualisation, decoration and signage work, advertising, film and television props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Driving a pile into the seabed is done by dropping a weight on it, thousands of times, with hydraulics deciding exactly how hard and how often. Every offshore wind turbine and every harbour wall in the world begins with this noise.
The model holds 95,762 polygons and 99,381 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits marine construction and offshore visualisation, equipment marketing, infrastructure presentation, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The small girl in a headscarf and long sarafan is a character design built entirely on silhouette. The proportions are exaggerated so she reads at any size, and the seated pose is the one animation uses when the character is about to cause trouble rather than while doing it.
The figure holds 116,780 polygons and 106,800 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in the sitting pose, and carries StemCell certification.
At $59 it suits animation and children's media, game characters, toy and merchandise visualisation, fan illustration and previsualisation. On sale since 2024.

The fast food cheeseburger is one of the most standardised objects ever produced. Same diameter, same order of components, same wrapper, in every country that has one, which is precisely why it is so recognisable as an image.
The model is very light at 13,200 polygons and 13,290 vertices, built in quads only with mixed UV layout, so it drops into any scene. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits food and beverage visualisation, packaging and menu imagery, advertising, restaurant and interior scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Ammunition and equipment boxes are designed to be stacked, dropped, and carried by two people who cannot see each other. The handles, the corners and the stencilled markings on them are all standardised for exactly that, which is why they look the way they do.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the boxes as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 the set suits defence and logistics visualisation, film and television set dressing, game environments, documentary work and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The refuelling boom is a wing with a nozzle on the end, flown by an operator lying at the back of the tanker. In flight configuration it is extended and steering itself into a receptacle a few metres away on an aircraft doing several hundred knots.
The model is light at 21,282 polygons and 21,627 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in the flight configuration. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits aviation and defence visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, animation sequences, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Deck mounted launchers are angled rather than vertical for a simple reason: the missile has to clear the ship before its own motor takes over, and the tilt buys those first few metres without any moving parts at all.
The model holds 95,474 polygons and 97,640 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 10 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits naval and defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The interactive display replaced the projector because the room no longer had to be dark. On a mobile stand it also stops belonging to one room, which is the difference between a fitted installation and a piece of equipment that gets used.
The model holds 69,022 polygons and 69,316 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the stand together with the screen. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits education and corporate interior visualisation, AV equipment marketing, classroom and meeting room scenes, product imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2025.

A power bank plugged into a phone is a specific narrative: the day has gone on longer than planned. Modular designs take that further by letting cells be added or swapped, which is a repairability argument as much as a capacity one.
The model is supplied with the power bank connected to the phone, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits product and technology visualisation, e-commerce and packaging imagery, advertising, lifestyle and desk scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Mosin was carried through both world wars and is still turning up in conflicts today, which makes it one of the longest serving rifles ever made. It is simple, heavy and almost impossible to break, and the sling threads through slots in the stock rather than swivels.
The model is light at 23,746 polygons and 24,638 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the sling. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits historical and documentary visualisation, period film and television props, game weapons, museum material, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

An upper stage is the part of a rocket that does the quiet work. The boosters get the noise and the photographs; this stage lights in vacuum, burns for a long time, and is what actually decides whether the payload reaches the orbit it was meant for.
The model holds 248,595 polygons and 253,513 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits space programme visualisation, news and documentary graphics, education and museum work, launch animation, film and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A rotary corn head does not care which way the rows are planted, which is the whole reason it exists. Conventional heads have to follow the rows; a rotary one takes the crop at any angle, and that turns a whole field into one continuous pass.

The model holds 297,020 polygons and 285,888 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in worn condition and rigged so it can be posed or animated. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits agricultural machinery marketing, harvest and farming visualisation, training material, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2023.

The briefcase is one of the most persistent images of the cold war and one of the least accurate. What such a case actually contains is communication equipment and authentication codes, not a weapon, but the shorthand has outlived every attempt to correct it.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the pieces as static items. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 the set suits film and television props, thriller and documentary production, game environments, editorial and historical illustration. On sale since 2025.
